The matching cascade, step by step

Source: vignettes/cascade-workflow.Rmd
cascade-workflow.Rmd

A 990-PF filer types a grantee’s name into Part XIV Table 3a by hand. There is no EIN, the name is often abbreviated or misspelled, and the address may be the grantee’s headquarters, a program site, a lockbox, or the foundation’s own office. pfmatch recovers the recipient’s EIN by running that text against the IRS Business Master File through a staged cascade: a sequence of blocking passes that start tight and loosen, each one only looking at what the previous passes could not settle.

Where the grants come from

Grants are the PF-P15-T01-SUPPLEMENTARY-INFO-GRANT-PAID table of the NCCS e-file (ef2) release, retrieved with pf_efilepf_fetch(), which delegates release resolution to panel990. Columns carry the concordance990 v2 research variable names, so the recipient name arrives as PF_15_G_PAID_RECIP_NAME_ORG_L1 rather than a positional or legacy label.

pf_efilepf_build() deduplicates superseded filings as it builds — identical filings collapse, an amended filing supersedes its original, and filings that disagree with no amendment to settle them are all kept and flagged. It removes 1.75% of grant rows corpus-wide and never drops a short-period return for sharing a tax year with a full-year one. Rows are addressed by OBJECTID | TABLE_ID, the published row key.

This article walks the passes in order and shows, for each, real cases that clear and real cases that are carried forward. Every number and name below comes from one run — 5,000 grant rows against the augmented unified reference (3,880,431 rows) — not from illustration.

The shape of it

The pfmatch cascade. Tight passes run first; only a YES removes a query from the pending queue, so MAYBE and NO are carried onward; and the final decision is made over the union of the candidates every pass contributed.

Two mechanics matter more than the pass list, and both are easy to get wrong.

Only YES leaves the queue. After each pass, np_cascade() removes a query from pending only if it reached the YES tier. MAYBE and NO stay in, so later and looser passes keep adding candidates for them. The queue goes 4,964 → 2,496 over the ten passes that fire.

The final decision is made over the union, not pass by pass. Every pass’s scored pairs are accumulated; at the end they are de-duplicated by (query, EIN), keeping the tightest pass that produced each, and np_select() / np_tier() run once over that union. So a pass can generate the winning candidate without being the pass that resolved the case.

That distinction explains an apparent contradiction between the two tables below. Pass C1 resolves zero queries at the moment it runs, yet one case is finally attributed to it — the candidate C1 generated won after later passes had contributed theirs.

Read the two together and the cascade’s economics are stark. Stage A buys 2,113 resolutions for 96,843 candidates. Stage B buys 328 for 1.1 million. Stage C buys nothing at all for 105,389 — and that is not bad luck, it is structural; see Why cross-state passes cannot clear below.

How a case is scored

Blocking only decides which pairs get looked at. The decision is:

score = 0.6 x name + 0.4 x geo
geo   = max(zip9 1.00, street 0.95, zip5 0.90, pobox 0.90,
            zip3 0.55, city 0.50, state 0.20)

YES    score >= 0.78  AND  margin >= 0.05
MAYBE  score >= 0.65
NO     below that

margin is the gap to the runner-up. It is the second half of the YES rule and it does most of the work of carrying cases forward, as the examples show.

Name similarity is floored: below jw_threshold (0.85) it contributes zero rather than a small amount, so a name that is merely not-very-similar is treated as no evidence at all.

Stage A — exact

Four passes, each an exact join on a composite key, differing in which key and which name version. They are cheap, they are the most precise thing available, and they do most of the work.

A1 · name + ZIP5

The tightest pass in the cascade: the normalized name and the 5-digit ZIP must both match exactly.

role tier filed name st matched BMF name score margin
carried forward MAYBE ST SAHAG ARMENIAN CHURCH MN SAINT SAHAG ARMENIAN CHURCH 0.98 0.00
carried forward MAYBE ST PETERS HOSPITAL FOUNDATION NY SAINT PETERS HOSPITAL FOUNDATION 0.98 0.02
clears (hard) YES METROPOLITAN OPERA GUILD INC NY METROPOLITAN OPERA GUILD 0.96 0.05
clears (regular) YES SAN FRANCISCO SYMPHONY CA SAN FRANCISCO SYMPHONY 0.98 0.98

SAN FRANCISCO SYMPHONY is the regular case — exact name, exact ZIP, nothing else close, margin 0.98.

METROPOLITAN OPERA GUILD INC is the hard version of the same shape. The name matches exactly after the corporate suffix is stripped, but the Metropolitan Opera family has several similarly named entities in one ZIP, so the margin falls to exactly 0.05 — the threshold. One notch lower and it would not have cleared.

The two carried-forward cases are the pattern worth internalising: both score 0.98 with a perfect name similarity, and are MAYBE anyway. ST SAHAG ARMENIAN CHURCH matched SAINT SAHAG ARMENIAN CHURCH with name_sim = 1.000, and its margin is 0.000 — a second reference row scored identically. Nothing is wrong with the name; there are simply two candidates the evidence cannot separate. That is a tie, not a failure, and it is the single most common reason a tight pass hands a case onward.

A2 · name + state

Loosens the geography from ZIP5 to state, which widens the candidate pool roughly fivefold (79,930 candidates against 16,093).

role tier filed name st matched BMF name score margin
carried forward MAYBE NASHVILLE BALLET TN NASHVILLE BALLET 0.98 0.00
carried forward MAYBE Wake Forest University NC WAKE FOREST UNIVERSITY 0.98 0.00
clears (hard) YES CARNEGIE MELLON UNIVERSITY PA CARNEGIE MELLON UNIVERSITY 0.90 0.08
clears (regular) YES ZOOLOGICAL SOCIETY OF MILW WI ZOOLOGICAL SOCIETY OF MILW 0.98 0.98

CARNEGIE MELLON UNIVERSITY is the instructive clear. Score 0.900, not 0.98 — the name is exact but only the state corroborates, so geo contributes 0.4 x 0.50 rather than 0.4 x 0.90. It still clears because the margin is 0.08.

NASHVILLE BALLET and Wake Forest University are carried forward on margin 0.000 again, and both have exact names. A state-level match cannot separate a university from its own foundation or medical centre.

A3 / A4 · the DBA cross-products

A3 matches the filed name against the reference’s DBA; A4 matches a filed DBA against the reference’s legal name. These recover organisations that transact under a name that is not their legal one.

role tier filed name st matched BMF name score margin
carried forward MAYBE UNIVERSITY OF MONTANA MT University Of Montana 0.98 0.00
carried forward MAYBE SUMMA FOUNDATION OH Summa Foundation 0.98 0.00
clears (hard) YES SYRACUSE UNIVERSITY NY Syracuse University 0.96 0.06
clears (regular) YES ARABIA SHRINERS TX Arabia Shriners 0.98 0.98
role tier filed name st matched BMF name score margin
clears (hard) YES ST JUDE’S CHILDREN’S RESEARCH TN SAINT JUDES CHILDRENS RESEARCH HOSPITAL 0.96 0.061
clears (regular) YES SANTA BARBARA TRUST FOR HISTORIC CA SANTA BARBARA TRUST FOR HISTORIC PRESERVATION 0.98 0.980

ST JUDE'S CHILDREN'S RESEARCH → SAINT JUDES CHILDRENS RESEARCH HOSPITAL is the characteristic A4 case: the filed string is the familiar public name, the reference row carries the legal one, and only the DBA path connects them.

A5 (dba == dba) produced no candidates at all on this run. It is retained because it costs nothing when it does not fire.

Stage B — shared token, same state

Where exactness fails, B blocks on a shared name token within state, using an inverted index with IDF-weighted pruning: a pair is kept only if its shared tokens carry enough information (min_pair_idf = 8), and tokens appearing in more than 25,000 reference records are dropped entirely. This is what makes the cascade scale — without it, every query would be compared against every same-state organisation.

role tier filed name st matched BMF name score margin
carried forward MAYBE BOYS AND GIRLS CLUB OF TAMPA BAY INC FL BOYS AND GIRLS CLUBS OF TAMPA BAY 0.974 0.000
carried forward MAYBE DENTAL LIFELINE NETWORK CO Dental Lifeline Network-Nc 0.966 -0.014
clears (hard) YES AMERICAN FRIENDS OF MAGEN DAVID ADOM NY AMERICAN FRIENDS OF MAGEN DAVID ADO 0.954 0.054
clears (regular) YES Friends of South Georgia Is CO FRIENDS OF SOUTH GEORGIA ISLAND 0.954 0.954
role tier filed name st matched BMF name score margin
carried forward MAYBE CAPITAL AREA FOODBANK DC CAPITAL AREA FOOD BANK 0.971 0.000
carried forward MAYBE UNITED NATIONS ASSOCIATION OF USA NY UNITED NATIONS ASSOCIATION OF THE USA 0.958 0.000
clears (hard) YES INTERNATIONAL CITY THEATRE (ICT) CA INTERNATIONAL CITY THEATRE 0.953 0.066
clears (regular) YES CARBON180 DC CARBON 180 0.960 0.960

B is where the first genuinely wrong answers appear, and where NO becomes a real outcome (547 and 60 cases). Two carried-forward cases show different mechanisms:

  • BOYS AND GIRLS CLUB OF TAMPA BAY INC → BOYS AND GIRLS CLUBS OF TAMPA BAY at 0.974 with margin 0.000. Almost certainly correct, held back by a tie — a chapter federation has many near-identical rows.
  • DENTAL LIFELINE NETWORK → Dental Lifeline Network-Nc with margin −0.014. A negative margin: the runner-up outscored the chosen candidate after the tie-break. The filer named the national body; the state affiliate scored higher. No amount of name similarity resolves that — it needs the grant’s purpose or the funder’s geography.

B2 adds de-spaced compounds as extra tokens, which is how CARBON180 reaches CARBON 180 and CAPITAL AREA FOODBANK reaches CAPITAL AREA FOOD BANK.

Stage C — exact name, any state

C drops the state requirement entirely, for the case where the filed address is a lockbox or the funder’s own office rather than the grantee’s.

role tier filed name st matched BMF name score margin
carried forward MAYBE HARRY S TRUMAN LIBRARY INSTITUTE VA HARRY S TRUMAN LIBRARY INSTITUTE 0.72 0.07
carried forward MAYBE MAKE A WISH FOUNDATION OH MAKE A WISH 0.72 0.00
clears (regular) YES NATIONAL WORLD WAR II MUSEUM CO NATIONAL WORLD WAR II MUSEUM 0.98 0.90
role tier filed name st matched BMF name score margin
carried forward NO HIGHER GROUND ID Higher Ground 0.6 0.00
carried forward NO ROSARY ACADEMY CA Rosary Academy 0.6 0.52

Why cross-state passes cannot clear

C1 and C2 generate 105,389 candidates and resolve zero. The reason is arithmetic, not data:

A cross-state pair has no geographic corroboration. The state conflict gate zeroes the city and ZIP3 terms deliberately — a shared city name across two states is a coincidence of naming, not evidence — so geo = 0 and

score = 0.6 x name + 0.4 x 0  <=  0.600

0.600 is below the 0.65 MAYBE floor, let alone the 0.78 YES threshold. A perfect cross-state name match cannot reach MAYBE on its own. HIGHER GROUND and ROSARY ACADEMY both sit at exactly 0.600 with name_sim = 1.000 and are NO. HARRY S TRUMAN LIBRARY INSTITUTE reaches 0.720 only because its state term fires.

So stage C does not function as an acceptance pass. It functions as a candidate supplier for adjudication: 152 cases finally attributed to C1 are MAYBE, meaning the cross-state candidate it surfaced became the best available answer once a reviewer looks. Whether 105,389 candidates is a fair price for 152 review candidates is a live question — a related unblocked token pass (C3) was measured and rejected for yielding zero YES.

Stage D — recovery

D runs last, on whatever remains, and addresses two specific filing habits.

D1 · acronym. Blocks on name_acro, which is the name key plus the record’s initials, so ICT can meet INTERNATIONAL CITY THEATRE and UCAP can meet URBAN COLLABORATIVE ACCELERATED PROGRAM.

D2 · truncated prefix. Blocks on the first 18 characters of the name plus an exact ZIP5. The prefix alone is far too blunt — AMERICAN ASSOCIATION OF PRO-LIFE OBSTETRICIANS and AMERICAN ASSOCIATION OF ZOO KEEPERS share one — so it is paired with the ZIP, and on the query side it fires only for names the parser flagged as actually cut off.

role tier filed name st matched BMF name score margin
carried forward MAYBE CONGREGATION SHAARE TEFILAH NY CONGREGATION SHAARA TEFILLE 0.900 0.000
carried forward MAYBE ART FOR AUTISM FL ARTS FOR AUTISM FOUNDATION 0.900 0.255
clears (hard) YES ST JOHN’S LUTHERAN CHILDCARE NY SAINT JOHN LUTHERAN CHURCH 0.896 0.132
clears (regular) YES ACCESS SPORTS AMERICA MA ACCESS SPORT AMERICA 0.970 0.750
role tier filed name st matched BMF name score margin
clears (regular) YES UKRAINIAN CATHOLIC EDUCATION FOUNDA NY UKRAINIAN CATHOLIC EDUCATION FOUNDATION 0.94 0.86

ACCESS SPORTS AMERICA → ACCESS SPORT AMERICA (singular/plural) and ST JOHN'S LUTHERAN CHILDCARE → SAINT JOHN LUTHERAN CHURCH are the regular and hard versions: the first is a one-character difference with a 0.75 margin; the second clears at 0.896 on a name similarity of only 0.894, carried by a strong address match, and is the kind of case where the childcare programme and the church may or may not be the same filer-intended payee.

CONGREGATION SHAARE TEFILAH → CONGREGATION SHAARA TEFILLE is a transliteration difference — two vowels — carried forward on a 0.000 margin because several transliterations of the same congregation name exist.

Why cases do not clear

Across all the carried-forward examples, three mechanisms account for nearly everything, and only the third is what most people picture:

  1. Ties. Score is high, name_sim is often exactly 1.000, and margin is 0.000. The right answer may well be in the list; the evidence cannot single it out. Dominant at stages A and B.
  2. The structural cap. No geographic corroboration means the score cannot exceed 0.600, so the case cannot reach MAYBE however good the name. Dominant at stage C.
  3. Genuine ambiguity. Parent against chapter, institution against its own foundation, operating entity against its endowment. These have two defensible answers and no amount of string comparison settles them.

This is why there is no automatic acceptance of the MAYBE tier. A rule of “ZIP5 agrees and margin ≥ 0.05” was measured at 100% precision on 18 cases, then at 72% on 200 fresh ones — because 79% of the cases it fired on were token-overlap matches, which the scorer deliberately caps below YES precisely because containment cannot separate a parent from a chapter.

What happens next

pf_adjudicate() builds the review sheet: per candidate, the BMF name and address, NTEE code and definition, activity text, subsection and assets, plus the grant purpose and the filing foundation’s own NTEE and state — and, for every candidate rather than only the top pick, the NTEEv2 description and the Form 990 Part III mission and programme text. Adding that text was measured to resolve 45 of 56 hard cases.

Two things to know before using it:

  • NONE is a correct and common answer. In a labelled sample, 24 of 82 hard cases had no correct candidate in the list at all. A reviewer who assumes one of the five is right manufactures false positives.
  • Prioritise by dollars. Grant amounts are heavily skewed; roughly 740 reviews covers 70% of the recoverable unresolved dollars.

To score a configuration rather than argue about its clear rate, see pf_evaluate() and pf_consistency().
